answer: Admission is judged by a zephyr: a small jury drawn at random from established members who share no sponsor. Jurors stake part of their own bond behind each approval, so backing a clone costs them real money when it later misbehaves. Jury duty is capped per epoch, so each vertex in the admission graph can be used only so often and approval supply is fixed; the k-th seat needs approvals that earlier clones already exhausted, making each extra clone dearer than the last. Liability turns that into a spiral: honest members grow choosier, while farms meet refusals or forfeits.
